notes.title: A charge is priced per unit of time
notes.detail: 'late_fee 1% of limit per day' grows with how long the money is outstanding, which prices time rather than a service. For a Shariah-compliant product this has to become a one-off service charge, or a fee tied to a real cost that does not accrue.

region.reading: The gap falls from 38.9% to 17.0% once income is held roughly still, so most of it is income reaching the decision through the policy's income rules rather than region itself. That is a product question - whether this product should serve lower incomes at all - not a defect in the rules.
region.not_a_verdict: This is a measurement, not a compliance opinion. Whether a variable is a legitimate business necessity is a legal question about the product, and nothing here can answer it.

discrimination.reading: Weak separation. A cutoff on this score will cut good and bad alike.
discrimination.caveat: Measured on the 2,531 borrowers who reached the scorecard. The 2,469 stopped by a gate are excluded, which flatters the figure whenever the gates are removing bad borrowers.

cutoff_sweep.in_sample_warning: The net-maximising threshold of 40 is chosen on the same 2,531 borrowers it is scored against. It is the best cutoff for this cohort's past, and an optimistic estimate for anyone it has not seen. Treat the shape of the curve as the finding, not the argmax.
